title: Indian contributions and the revival beat
summary: Dance asks about Native American influence; Ramirez ties Jazz to church revival beat with hand-clapping accents.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Sure. But you touched on something there that interests me when you said out West the Indians... Now, we always hear about Jazz as a Negro, mainly Negro music.

But if you read history, all in that... Especially in the South at least, the Blacks and Indians intermarried extensively. Well, you know lots of Jazz musicians who are part Indian; you know, the mother was Cherokee or something. Now, it must be somewhere in there contributions from the Indians to that music. I mean, just as we know that in New Orleans, say, that the Black music is influenced by European music because they were exposed to it a lot, the Indian contribution is in there somewhere -- but we don't know where.

Oh yeah! It was all part of it. Especially in the old days with movies, when so-called the railroad was... In the old films, you know, the Indians were waiting at the so-called... The actors who were made up as Indians were waiting to attack the White settlers. All of a sudden you hear, 'Whoo-ooo,' BOOM-BOOM-BOOM-BOOM... And I would say it was kind of Oriental, too, you know, in character. But that was their sound; it comes from the drums, from their drums. Although their rhythmic patterns were different. But they hopped up and down to the drums,

just like African rhythms.
I mean, you wouldn't say the American Negro...their Jazz was more of a revival sound, which had to do with the church. Just like they imitated their masters in the plantations, dancing with... I mean, it seems to me like the Irish clog or whatever they were doing, the Blacks imitated. I mean, so goes the tale. I didn't live in those times, but it seems evident. But I mean, insofar as... Their beat is more a revival beat, with hand-clapping. It gives the accent on the second beat and the fourth beat, you stomp, and your foot will give you the pulse, you know, and then the after-beat... That's what seems to me a revival.
